item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Trump Says Iran Wants to Resume Talks
item.summary: The president did not say whether the United States had agreed to negotiate again. The U.S. military is blocking ships entering or leaving Iranian ports or coastal areas, in an effort to cut off Iran’s oil income.

item.title: Israelis Don’t Feel Much Like Victors in War With Iran
item.summary: The regime in Iran has not changed and the nuclear and missile threats have not been eliminated, leaving many Israelis to wonder what this was all for.

item.title: To Fill Drone Force Ranks, Russia Targets a New Demographic: Students
item.summary: Recruitment sessions have taken place at hundreds of universities and colleges across the country.

item.title: For Months, Pope Avoided Clash With Trump. Now He’s Clapping Back.
item.summary: President Trump lashed out on Sunday night at Pope Leo XIV, who responded hours later by saying he would continue to oppose war.

item.title: Trump Said Other Countries Would Help Blockade Iran. So Far, There Are No Takers.
item.summary: President Trump’s announcement of a complete U.S. blockade was his latest effort to pressure Iran to negotiate after direct talks over the weekend did not yield an agreement.

item.title: Iran Blockade Sets Up a Test of Which Side Can Endure More Pain
item.summary: President Trump is trying to choke off the country’s lifeline with a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. But the Iranians are betting that his tolerance for political pain is limited.

item.title: ‘The Strangest Sleepover Ever’: Dutch Skeptical as Their Royals Visit Trump
item.summary: The Dutch king and queen are set to stay at the White House on Monday night. At a time of trans-Atlantic tension, the Netherlands isn’t sure how it feels about that.

item.title: Orban Loss May Ease Hungary’s Tensions with European Union
item.summary: Prime Minister Viktor Orban has stymied the European Union for years, and particularly in recent months. Peter Magyar’s election could change that.
